Only with `--dry-run`. A stored project memory warns that in staging `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. Without the flag, the script would write to prod.

The script does support the flag (`scripts/export.py:8`), so this is the safe form:

```
python scripts/export.py --env staging --dry-run
```

I haven't run it. I only read the script. I'm also assuming the argument is `--env`, since the script uses `args.env`. Check the exact argument name against the script before running it.

The script only prints the bucket and the dry-run state in the lines I checked. I didn't read the rest of the file. Before relying on `--dry-run`, confirm that it skips every write to the bucket.

If you need a real, non-dry-run test, set `EXPORT_BUCKET` to a safe bucket first. The script falls back to `ledgerline-exports-dev` when the variable is unset.
